title: Exam Cram
subject: digestive-system
subtitle: Chapter 24 | Instructor-Aligned Rapid Review
introMarkdown: Short, test-oriented facts from the Chapter 24 physiology lecture and digestive anatomy-model slides. Memorize the bold terms, their functions, and the labeled structures.

sections.title: Seven Functions — Use the Instructor’s List
sections.markdown:
- **Ingestion:** Food enters mouth.
- **Mechanical processing:** Chewing, mixing, churning.
- **Chemical digestion:** Enzymes break molecules down.
- **Secretion:** Acid, enzymes, water, mucus, buffers, salts, bile.
- **Absorption:** Nutrients/ions/water into blood or lymph.
- **Compaction:** Water removed; feces concentrate.
- **Defecation:** Feces eliminated.

**Important:** Slides list **compaction**, not motility, as one of the seven. **Motility** is still the general term for muscular mixing and movement.

sections.title: Key Terms and Movement
sections.markdown:
- **Digestion:** Breakdown for absorption. **Catabolism:** Breaks down. **Anabolism:** Builds up.
- **Bolus:** Chewed, saliva-coated food. **Chyme:** Stomach's soupy mixture.
- **Mastication:** Chewing. **Deglutition:** Swallowing.
- **Peristalsis:** Propels forward. **Segmentation:** Mixes back and forth.
- **Mass movements:** Strong, infrequent colonic propulsion. **Haustral churning:** Local colon mixing.
- **Mesentery:** Double peritoneal fold carrying vessels, nerves, lymphatics.
- **Retroperitoneal:** Behind parietal peritoneum (e.g., most pancreas/duodenum).
- **Enterohepatic circulation:** Ileum reabsorbs bile salts → portal blood → liver.
- **Epiploic appendages:** Fat tags on colon. **Feces:** Compacted waste. **Flatus:** Gas.

sections.title: GI Wall and Peritoneum
sections.markdown:
- **Mucosa:** Innermost lining; secretion/absorption.
- **Submucosa:** Connective tissue, large vessels, nerves/lymphatics.
- **Muscularis externa:** Inner circular + outer longitudinal muscle; peristalsis.
- **Serosa:** Outer visceral peritoneal covering. **Adventitia:** Anchors structures (e.g., esophagus).
- **Myenteric plexus:** Motility. **Submucosal plexus:** Secretion/local blood flow.
- **Parietal peritoneum:** Abdominal wall. **Visceral:** Organ surface.
- **Lesser omentum:** Liver ↔ lesser stomach curvature.
- **Greater omentum:** Hangs from greater curvature; drapes over intestines.
- **Mesentery proper:** Small intestine. **Mesocolon:** Colon.

sections.title: Oral Cavity, Saliva, and Teeth
sections.markdown:
- **Mouth functions:** Sensory analysis, chewing, lubrication, initial chemical digestion, bolus formation.
- **Tongue:** Moves food; associated glands secrete **lingual lipase**. **Extrinsic muscles:** Gross movement. **Intrinsic:** Shape changes.
- **Parotid:** Near ear; **Stensen's duct**. **Submandibular:** Beneath jaw; **Wharton's duct**. **Sublingual:** Beneath tongue; small **Rivinus ducts**.
- **Saliva:** Mucins = lubrication; **amylase** = starch; **bicarbonate** = buffering; **lysozyme + IgA** = defense.
- **Fauces:** Mouth-to-throat opening. **Uvula:** Soft-palate tip. **Vestibule:** Lips/cheeks ↔ teeth.
- **Superior/inferior labium:** Upper/lower lip. **Dorsum:** Top of tongue.
- **Lingual frenulum:** Tongue to mouth floor. **Labial frenulum:** Lip to gums.
- **Tooth:** Crown, neck, root; **enamel** over crown; **cementum** over root; **dentin** underneath; **pulp cavity/root canal** contain nerves and vessels; **apical foramen** at root tip.
- **Periodontal ligament:** Root cementum to alveolar bone.
- **Teeth:** **Incisors** cut, **canines** tear, **premolars** crush, **molars** grind. **20 deciduous**, up to **32 permanent**.

sections.title: Pharynx, Esophagus, and Swallowing
sections.markdown:
- **Nasopharynx:** Air only. **Oropharynx/laryngopharynx:** Food and air passage.
- **Buccal/oral phase:** **Voluntary**; tongue pushes bolus backward.
- **Pharyngeal phase:** **Involuntary**; palatal/pharyngeal tactile receptors trigger reflex; soft palate rises, **larynx elevates**, airway protected.
- **Esophageal phase:** **Involuntary**; peristalsis moves bolus into stomach.
- **Coordinator:** **Medulla (brainstem)**.
- **Upper esophageal sphincter:** Helps prevent air entry. **Lower/cardiac sphincter:** Helps resist reflux.
- **Esophageal hiatus:** Opening through diaphragm. **Adventitia:** Outer anchoring layer of most esophagus.

sections.title: Stomach: Regions, Cells, and Functions
sections.markdown:
- **Slide lists five functions:** Food **storage**, **mechanical** mixing, **chemical** digestion, **intrinsic factor** production, **chyme delivery** to small intestine.
- **Four regions:** **Cardia → fundus → body → pylorus**.
- **Rugae:** Expandable folds. **Lesser/greater curvatures:** Short/long borders.
- **Muscle layers:** **Oblique + circular + longitudinal**; mix food.
- **Pyloric sphincter:** Controls chyme into duodenum.
- **Parietal cells:** **HCl + intrinsic factor**. HCl helps denature proteins, kills many microbes, activates pepsin.
- **Chief cells:** **Pepsinogen** (→ pepsin) + gastric lipase.
- **G cells:** **Gastrin** (increases gastric activity). **D cells:** **Somatostatin** (inhibits gastrin/acid).
- **Mucous cells:** Mucus + bicarbonate barrier protects stomach lining.
- **Lecture pH:** Approximately **1.5–2** in highly acidic gastric juice.

sections.title: Three Phases of Gastric Regulation
sections.markdown:
- **Cephalic:** Sight/smell/taste/thought of food → **vagus nerve** → stomach secretions.
- **Gastric:** Food/stomach stretch + peptides → **gastrin**, acid, enzymes, mixing.
- **Intestinal:** Chyme/acid/fat enter duodenum → **enterogastric inhibition**, slows acid secretion and gastric emptying.
- **Gastroileal reflex:** Stomach activity helps increase ileal movement/ileocecal passage.
- **Enteric nervous system + CNS + hormones:** Coordinate these phases.

sections.title: GI Hormones and Their Triggers
sections.markdown:
- **Gastrin — G cells:** Food, peptides, stretch → **increases gastric activity**.
- **CCK — I cells:** Fats/proteins in SI → **pancreatic enzymes + gallbladder contraction**, slows gastric emptying.
- **Secretin — S cells:** Acid in duodenum → **pancreatic bicarbonate**, slows gastric acid.
- **GIP — K cells:** Glucose/fats in SI → **glucose-dependent insulin release**; can inhibit gastric activity.
- **Somatostatin — D cells:** Gastric acidity → **inhibits gastrin and acid**.
- **VIP — enteric neurons:** **Dilates intestinal vessels**; supports secretion and intestinal activity (lecture emphasizes blood flow/absorption).

**Memorize first:** Gastrin = acid; CCK = enzymes/bile; secretin = bicarbonate; GIP = insulin; somatostatin = inhibition; VIP = vasodilation.

sections.title: Small Intestine: Regions and Absorption
sections.markdown:
- **Small intestine:** Major site of chemical digestion and nutrient absorption (lecture: ~**90%** of nutrient absorption).
- **Duodenum:** Receives chyme + bile + pancreatic enzymes/bicarbonate; neutralizes acid; **Brunner's glands** secrete alkaline mucus.
- **Jejunum:** Most nutrient absorption; prominent plicae and long villi; **lactase, maltase, sucrase** at brush border.
- **Ileum:** Absorbs **B12 + bile salts**; **Peyer's patches**; ends at **ileocecal valve**.
- **Plicae circulares:** Permanent folds; slow chyme/increase surface area.
- **Villi:** Mucosal projections with blood capillaries and **lacteals**.
- **Microvilli/brush border:** Enzymes + maximal membrane surface.
- **Enterocytes:** Absorb nutrients. **Paneth cells:** Lysozyme/defensins. **Goblet cells:** Mucus.
- **Crypts of Lieberkühn:** Intestinal gland depressions; Paneth cells near bases.
- **Fat pathway:** Micelles → enterocyte → **chylomicron** → **lacteal** → lymph → blood.

sections.title: Pancreas: Enzymes, Ducts, and Disease
sections.markdown:
- **Head:** In duodenal C-loop. **Body:** Behind stomach. **Tail:** Toward spleen.
- **Exocrine acini:** Digestive enzymes. **Endocrine islets:** Insulin/glucagon.
- **Amylase:** Carbs. **Proteases:** Proteins. **Lipase:** Fats. **Nucleases:** DNA/RNA.
- **Protease examples:** Trypsin, chymotrypsin, carboxypeptidase, elastase.
- **Duct cells:** Bicarbonate to neutralize stomach acid.
- **Main pancreatic duct (Wirsung):** Delivers juices to **duodenum**; **accessory duct (Santorini)** may also drain pancreas.
- **Pancreatitis:** Inflamed pancreas; gallstones obstructing drainage and alcohol are major causes.

sections.title: Liver, Gallbladder, and Bile Flow
sections.markdown:
- **Liver:** Makes bile, processes blood nutrients, stores glycogen/vitamins/iron, metabolizes toxins, makes plasma proteins, handles bilirubin.
- **Hepatocytes:** Metabolism + bile. **Kupffer cells:** Sinusoidal macrophages. **Sinusoids:** Exchange between blood and liver cells.
- **Liver lobes:** **Right, left, caudate, quadrate**. **Falciform ligament:** Anterior landmark. **Round ligament:** Fetal umbilical-vein remnant.
- **Gallbladder:** Stores/concentrates bile; **CCK** triggers contraction.
- **Bile:** **Emulsifies fat**; no digestive enzymes. **Enterohepatic circulation:** Bile salts recycled from terminal ileum to liver.
- **Duct sequence:** Right + left hepatic ducts → **common hepatic duct**; + **cystic duct** → **common bile duct**.
- **Release:** Gallbladder → cystic duct → common bile duct → often joins main pancreatic duct → **hepatopancreatic ampulla** → **major duodenal papilla** → **descending duodenum**.
- **Sphincter of Oddi:** Regulates bile/pancreatic juice entry.

sections.title: Large Intestine and Defecation
sections.markdown:
- **Three functions:** Water absorption/compaction, some vitamin-related absorption, storage/elimination of feces.
- **Path:** **Cecum → ascending → right (hepatic) flexure → transverse → left (splenic) flexure → descending → sigmoid → rectum → anus**.
- **Appendix:** Projects from cecum. **Ileocecal valve:** SI–LI junction.
- **Haustra:** Colon pouches. **Taeniae coli:** Longitudinal muscle bands causing sacculations. **Epiploic appendages:** Fat tags.
- **Large intestine has no villi**; abundant goblet cells and bacteria.
- **Cecum → transverse:** Slow mixing/transit, water recovery. **Transverse → rectum:** Occasional **mass movements**, further fecal compaction (patterns overlap).
- **Rectal stretch → defecation reflex:** Local enteric + sacral reflexes; **internal sphincter** = involuntary smooth muscle; **external** = voluntary skeletal muscle.
- **Flatus:** Intestinal gas; **feces:** Compacted waste.

sections.title: Instructor-Named Disorders
sections.markdown:
- **Mumps:** Viral infection/swelling of parotid glands. **Gingivitis:** Inflamed gums. **Periodontal disease:** Damaged tooth-supporting tissues.
- **Esophagitis:** Esophageal inflammation. **Gastritis:** Stomach inflammation. **Peptic ulcer:** Gastric/duodenal mucosal ulceration.
- **Enteritis:** Small-intestine inflammation. **Gastroenteritis:** Stomach/intestine inflammation.
- **Giardiasis:** *Giardia* infection/diarrhea. **Dysentery:** Diarrhea with blood (often mucus).
- **Hepatitis:** Inflamed liver. **Cirrhosis:** Liver scarring. **Jaundice:** Bilirubin-related yellowing.
- **Gallstones:** Biliary deposits. **Cholecystitis:** Gallbladder inflammation. **Pancreatitis:** Pancreatic inflammation.
- **Colitis:** Colon inflammation. **Cholera:** *V. cholerae* causes profuse watery diarrhea.
- **Constipation:** Slow/hard stool. **Diarrhea:** Loose watery stool. **Diverticulitis:** Inflamed diverticula.
- **Polyps:** Some are precancerous; potential link to **colorectal cancer**.

sections.title: Anatomy Model: Identification Checklist
sections.markdown:
- **Oral cavity:** Uvula, fauces, superior/inferior labium, labial/lingual frenulum, dorsum, vestibule, parotid/sublingual/submandibular glands.
- **Tooth:** Crown, neck, root, enamel, dentin, pulp cavity, root canal, cementum, apical foramen, periodontal ligament.
- **Stomach:** Cardia, fundus, body, pylorus, pyloric sphincter, lesser/greater curvature, rugae, oblique/circular/longitudinal muscles.
- **Pancreas:** Head, body, tail, main pancreatic duct, accessory duct, duodenum.
- **Liver/biliary:** Right/left/caudate/quadrate lobes, falciform/round ligament, gallbladder, right/left/common hepatic duct, cystic duct, common bile duct.
- **Small intestine:** Duodenum, jejunum, ileum, plicae, villi, intestinal crypt, lacteal, Peyer's patches, ileocecal valve.
- **Large intestine:** Cecum, appendix, ascending/transverse/descending/sigmoid colon, hepatic/splenic flexures, haustra, taeniae coli, rectum, internal/external anal sphincters.

sections.title: Rapid Recall — Likely Exam Associations
sections.markdown:
- **Seven functions include?** Compaction, not motility, in the lecture list.
- **Voluntary swallowing phase?** Buccal/oral. **Coordinator?** Medulla.
- **Propels food?** Peristalsis. **Mixes chyme?** Segmentation.
- **HCl + intrinsic factor?** Parietal. **Pepsinogen?** Chief.
- **Gastrin?** G cell. **Somatostatin?** D cell.
- **Acid in duodenum?** Secretin. **Fats/protein in SI?** CCK.
- **Glucose-triggered insulin release?** GIP. **Intestinal vasodilation?** VIP.
- **Pancreatic enzymes?** Acini. **Pancreatic bicarbonate?** Ducts.
- **Antimicrobial SI cells?** Paneth. **Immune nodules in ileum?** Peyer's patches.
- **B12 and bile salts?** Terminal ileum. **Chylomicron vessel?** Lacteal.
- **Duodenal alkaline-mucus glands?** Brunner's.
- **Liver macrophages?** Kupffer. **Functional liver cells?** Hepatocytes.
- **Bile storage?** Gallbladder. **Bile job?** Emulsification.
- **Bile + pancreatic ducts open into?** Descending duodenum (major papilla).
- **Sphincter controlling bile/pancreatic entry?** Oddi.
- **Colon longitudinal bands?** Taeniae coli. **Colon pouches?** Haustra.
- **Voluntary anal sphincter?** External. **Involuntary?** Internal.
